meta.title: KIRIN AI Tools Repository
meta.audience: Foster Hybrid MBA students new to AI

categories.title: 💬 General-Purpose Assistants
categories.blurb: Start here. These are the Swiss-army tools that handle writing, analysis, brainstorming, summarizing, and light coding in one chat box. Pick ONE as your daily driver before reaching for anything specialized.

categories.title: 🔎 Research & Literature
categories.blurb: Cited answers, paper discovery, and synthesis of sources. Use these when "I need evidence" matters more than "I need a draft."

categories.title: ✍️ Writing & Editing
categories.blurb: Polish, paraphrase, and clarity. These refine what you've written rather than replace your thinking.

categories.title: 📊 Data Analysis & Visualization
categories.blurb: Turn spreadsheets and datasets into analysis and dashboards — from chat-based analysts to enterprise BI.

categories.title: 🖼️ Image, Design & Brand
categories.blurb: Generate visuals, graphics, and brand assets. Watch licensing for anything you publish.

categories.title: 🎤 Presentations & Slides
categories.blurb: Get a first-draft deck in minutes. Always rework AI slides before presenting — they read as generic out of the box.

categories.title: 🎧 Audio & Voice
categories.blurb: Turn text into audio and audio into text. Listen to readings on your commute, or generate clean voiceovers for presentations.

categories.title: 🎙️ Meetings & Note-Taking
categories.blurb: Transcribe lectures and team calls, capture action items, and organize notes. Get consent before recording others.

categories.title: ⚙️ Productivity & Workflow Automation
categories.blurb: Connect your apps and kill repetitive busywork.

categories.title: 💻 Coding & Technical
categories.blurb: For the analytics, data, and tech-track electives — or anyone learning to build.

categories.title: 💼 Career & Recruiting
categories.blurb: Résumés, networking, interview prep, and application tracking.

categories.title: 🛡️ Governance, Responsible Use & Compliance
categories.blurb: The part most tool lists skip. Read the Ground Rules on the site before using anything above in graded work.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.what: Conversational assistant for writing, analysis, brainstorming, and light coding; built-in data analysis, image generation, and web browsing.
tools.best_for: A reliable all-rounder and most people's first tool.
tools.pricing: Free (ad-supported in the US since Feb 2026); Go $8/mo, Plus $20/mo, Pro $100–200/mo
tools.notes: Free tier is enough for most coursework. Verify before pasting anything confidential.

tools.name: Claude
tools.what: Conversational assistant especially strong at long-document analysis, careful reasoning, and natural writing.
tools.best_for: Nuanced writing, reading large PDFs/case packs, and work where tone matters.
tools.notes: Large context window handles full case packs in one go.

tools.name: Google Gemini
tools.what: Google's assistant with a very large context window, deeply integrated into Gmail, Docs, Drive, and Sheets; also generates images.
tools.best_for: Students who live in Google Workspace; fits an entire semester of notes in context.
tools.pricing: Free; AI Plus $7.99/mo, AI Pro $19.99/mo — free for ~1 year for verified students
tools.notes: Student year free via google.com/students — strong value.

tools.name: Microsoft Copilot
tools.what: Microsoft's assistant, embedded across Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Teams.
tools.best_for: Office-heavy workflows where you want AI inside the apps you already use.
tools.pricing: Free chat; M365 Copilot is a paid add-on (check school licensing)
tools.notes: Foster/UW may provide M365 Copilot access — check before paying.

tools.name: Perplexity
tools.what: AI answer engine that searches the live web and returns sourced, cited answers.
tools.best_for: Cited research, fact-checking, and current-events questions where a citation trail matters.
tools.pricing: Free; Pro $20/mo; Education Pro $4.99/mo (free ~1 year for verified students)
tools.notes: .gov / some .mil emails get a free Pro year with zero data retention — relevant for veterans/feds.

tools.name: NotebookLM
tools.what: Grounded research assistant that answers only from sources YOU upload; generates summaries, study guides, and podcast-style audio overviews.
tools.best_for: Synthesizing assigned readings and case packs with minimal hallucination.
tools.notes: Its audio-overview feature turns your sources into a two-host podcast — great for the commute.

tools.name: Elicit
tools.what: Research assistant that finds academic papers and extracts findings into comparison tables.
tools.best_for: Literature reviews and evidence synthesis for term papers.
tools.pricing: Free tier; paid plans for higher volume

tools.name: Consensus
tools.what: Search engine that surfaces conclusions from peer-reviewed research for a given question.
tools.best_for: Quickly answering "what does the research say about X?" with citations.

tools.name: SciSpace
tools.what: Reads and explains dense academic papers, clarifies jargon and math, and supports literature search.
tools.best_for: Getting through technical PDFs you'd otherwise bounce off.

tools.name: Grammarly
tools.what: Grammar, clarity, and tone checking, plus generative drafting and rewriting help.
tools.best_for: Polishing assignments, emails, and professional communication.

tools.name: QuillBot
tools.what: Paraphrasing, summarizing, grammar checking, and citation generation.
tools.best_for: Tightening and rephrasing drafts without changing meaning.
tools.notes: Paraphrasing to dodge a detector is not a free pass — disclosure rules still apply.

tools.name: Jasper
tools.what: Marketing and brand copy generation at scale with reusable brand-voice profiles.
tools.best_for: Marketing electives and content/brand projects.

tools.name: Julius AI
tools.what: Chat-based data analyst — upload a dataset, ask questions in plain English, get charts and statistics.
tools.best_for: Analyzing CSVs/Excel without writing formulas or code.

tools.name: Excel + Copilot
tools.what: Natural-language formulas, analysis, and chart generation inside Excel.
tools.best_for: Spreadsheet analysis when you'd rather describe the task than build the formula.
tools.pricing: Excel paid; Copilot in Excel requires M365 Copilot

tools.name: Microsoft Power BI
tools.what: Business-intelligence dashboards with a Copilot for natural-language reporting; integrates tightly with Excel.
tools.best_for: Enterprise-style reporting and dashboards for projects and capstones.
tools.pricing: Power BI Desktop free; Pro paid (student options via Microsoft)

tools.name: Tableau
tools.what: Industry-standard visual analytics platform with AI-assisted insights.
tools.best_for: Serious data viz and analytics-track work; a résumé-worthy skill.
tools.pricing: Paid; free 1-year license for students via Tableau Academic

tools.name: Canva
tools.what: Design platform with AI (Magic Studio) for slides, social graphics, and image generation.
tools.best_for: Producing polished visuals and decks with zero design background.
tools.pricing: Free; Pro paid (free for some students/educators)

tools.name: Adobe Firefly
tools.what: Generative image tool trained for commercial safety, integrated with Adobe apps.
tools.best_for: Brand-safe imagery you intend to publish or reuse.
tools.notes: Marketed as commercially safer than open image generators — relevant for brand work.

tools.name: Midjourney
tools.what: High-quality generative image creation from text prompts.
tools.best_for: Original, striking imagery for projects and pitches.

tools.name: Ideogram
tools.what: Image generation with best-in-class legible text rendering — posters, logos, and graphics with words in them.
tools.best_for: Branded graphics and social images where the text has to look right.

tools.name: Gamma
tools.what: Generates full slide decks, docs, and simple webpages from a prompt or outline.
tools.best_for: Getting a first-draft deck in minutes, then editing.

tools.name: Copilot in PowerPoint
tools.what: Builds and redesigns slides from prompts inside PowerPoint.
tools.best_for: Office users who want AI slides in the tool they already present from.

tools.name: Speechify
tools.what: Text-to-speech that reads articles, PDFs, and assigned readings aloud in natural voices, at your own speed.
tools.best_for: Listening to reading assignments on the commute instead of reading them.
tools.pricing: Free tier; Premium paid (student pricing available)
tools.notes: A cohort favorite for turning case readings into audio. Pairs well with NotebookLM's audio overviews.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.what: High-quality AI voice generation and text-to-speech for narration and voiceovers.
tools.best_for: Clean voiceover for presentation videos and recorded walkthroughs.

tools.name: Otter.ai
tools.what: Live transcription with AI-generated meeting and lecture notes and summaries.
tools.best_for: Transcribing classes and capturing what was said in real time.

tools.name: Fireflies.ai
tools.what: Records, transcribes, and summarizes meetings across Zoom, Meet, and Teams; searchable archive and action items.
tools.best_for: Team-project meetings — auto-captured notes and to-dos.
tools.notes: Tell participants they're being recorded before it joins.

tools.name: Notion AI
tools.what: AI built into Notion for notes, task management, summaries, and project docs in one workspace.
tools.best_for: Keeping notes, study plans, and group projects organized in a single place.

tools.name: Zapier
tools.what: Connects 6,000+ apps to automate multi-step workflows, now with AI steps and agents.
tools.best_for: Automating repetitive cross-app tasks (e.g., form to sheet to email).

tools.name: Make
tools.what: Visual, node-based automation platform — a flexible Zapier alternative.
tools.best_for: More complex automations on a tighter budget.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.what: AI pair-programmer that autocompletes and explains code inside your editor.
tools.best_for: Coding assignments and learning to program.
tools.pricing: Free for verified students (Copilot Student, launched Mar 2026)
tools.notes: Verify through the GitHub Student Developer Pack.

tools.name: Cursor
tools.what: An AI-first code editor that can read and edit your whole project conversationally.
tools.best_for: Building apps, scripts, or analyses with heavy AI assistance.
tools.pricing: Free tier; Pro paid (student discount available)

tools.name: LinkedIn (AI features)
tools.what: AI-assisted profile and résumé feedback, job matching, and interview prep.
tools.best_for: Networking, internship/job search, and positioning.

tools.name: Teal
tools.what: Résumé builder and job-application tracker with AI tailoring to job postings.
tools.best_for: Tailoring résumés to specific roles and tracking applications in one place.
tools.notes: Pair with a general assistant to draft STAR interview stories.

tools.name: Your course / Foster AI policy
tools.what: The single most important "tool" here — the AI-use rules for each specific course and assignment.
tools.best_for: Knowing what's allowed before you use anything else on this list.
tools.notes: Rules vary by course and instructor. When in doubt, ask and disclose.

tools.name: APA AI Citation Guidance
tools.what: How to cite and disclose AI assistance in academic work.
tools.best_for: Getting disclosure right — undisclosed use carries the heaviest penalties.

tools.name: Turnitin (awareness)
tools.what: Plagiarism and AI-writing detection used by many institutions.
tools.best_for: Understanding how submissions may be screened — and that detectors produce false positives.
tools.pricing: Institutional (used by your school, not bought by you)
tools.notes: Proactive disclosure beats arguing with a detector after the fact.

tools.name: Credo AI
tools.what: Enterprise AI governance platform — policy packs, generative-AI guardrails, and audit trails.
tools.best_for: Anyone exploring AI risk, GRC, or compliance as a career direction.
tools.notes: Included as a career-relevant signal of where enterprise AI governance is heading.
